summary: Refactor regression testing (server.py helper extraction + use-toast.js deps=[] + STALE_TIME_MS constant). Backend 35/35 pytest pass across 3 test files (backend_test.py 15/15, test_chunked_upload.py 12/12, new test_refactor.py 8/8). New tests explicitly cover the refactor spec items: /api/ health, /api/config (no-auth, includes color_accent/year/logo_text), direct POST /api/admin/upload 415 when kind=video with image content-type, chunked upload response shape ({complete:false,chunk_index,received_bytes} vs {complete:true,url,size,id}) with on-disk byte-exact reassembly + SHA verification, Range 206 (1024 bytes for bytes=0-1023) + Accept-Ranges on 200 + HEAD (Content-Length/Content-Type/Accept-Ranges), admin settings roundtrip (color_accent/color_bg/color_text/logo_text/footer_text/year/socials all persist via GET after PUT), season DELETE cascades episodes. Frontend: /login.html → correct code → 302 to /, 11 episode cards rendered (Staffel/Reise text present). /admin.html → admin password → dashboard visible with Videos + Einstellungen + Sicherheit tabs, stats 7 episodes / 1 Staffel / 2 Länder / 19 media. No functional regression detected — refactor is behavior-preserving.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _resolve_kind: clean separation of MIME validation — good. Consider adding magic-byte sniffing (python-magic) for defense-in-depth; current header-only trust matches existing behavior.
server.py _validate_chunk_params: extension check is robust (Path.suffix.lower()). Consider ALSO validating filename length + non-empty; currently a filename of just '.mp4' would pass.
server.py _iter_file_range: reads 1 MB per iteration — fine for streaming. Not backpressure-aware but acceptable for FastAPI+Uvicorn.

server.py _check_upload_auth: still resolves fname directly under UPLOAD_DIR without a path-traversal guard (Path.resolve().is_relative_to(UPLOAD_DIR)). Not exploitable through Starlette path parsing today but worth hardening. Also flagged in iteration_2.

server.py seed_defaults composer + _seed_* helpers: idempotency logic is per-helper (each early-returns if the collection already has documents). Correct behavior preserved — verified against live DB where user has customized settings (series_title='unwritten') and reduced to 7 episodes / 2 countries: seed did NOT re-inject or overwrite.
frontend use-toast.js useEffect deps=[]: correct — setState identity from useState is stable, no need to include it. eslint-disable comment is in place.
frontend index.js STALE_TIME_MS: extracted as a module const — good. Consider moving to a shared constants file if reused.

context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini pins -n 2 --dist loadscope. Live DB in test_database has been customized by the user (series_title='unwritten', 7 non-hidden episodes across 2 countries). Do NOT re-hardcode seed values in assertions — assert structure, not exact seed content. seed_defaults() is per-collection idempotent and safe to trigger on startup. Login-attempts brute-force lockout can cascade across xdist workers when tests using 'wrong code' run in parallel with fixture-based viewer/admin logins; test_refactor.py has a defensive _clear_lockout() before the viewer fixture. If chunked upload retest is needed, the endpoint contract now verified: first N-1 chunks → {ok:true, complete:false, chunk_index, received_bytes}; final chunk → {ok:true, complete:true, url:/api/uploads/videos/<id>_<name>, size, id, kind}.
rca of the issue: No refactor regression. Two pre-existing test assertions in backend_test.py::test_11_content_seed were tied to seed defaults (series_title='Meine Weltreise', 18 episodes, 3 specific country names) but the live DB reflects user edits since the last iteration (title customized to 'unwritten', episodes trimmed to 7, countries reduced to 2). The seed_defaults() refactor is per-collection idempotent by design — it did not overwrite user data. Fixed the tests to assert structural invariants rather than seed content.
